title: Harmonize focus treatments, ARIA for grouped controls, and low-contrast legend fixes for VPAT submission
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: As part of the Q2 VPAT readiness push we discovered inconsistent focus visuals across tokenized components, ambiguous ARIA usage in composite controls (segmented groups, toolbar-like action groups), and several chart legend / table label color ramps that fall under WCAG failures for low-contrast scenarios. This ticket consolidates the design decisions and implementation tasks to surface a single, testable deliverable for the VPAT annex.
scope: Audit and remediate focus ring styles (all tokens), normalize ARIA semantics for grouped controls (radio groups, segmented controls, action toolbars), and update chart legend and dense table label color ramps to meet WCAG AA contrast for regular text (4.5:1) and large text (3:1). Include Storybook snapshots and automated axe checks. Do not touch alternative interaction patterns (e.g., mobile-specific gestures) in this ticket.
out_of_scope: Native mobile components, third-party charting library internal rendering (we will create wrappers where needed but not contribute upstream), and color palette brand refresh.
acceptance_criteria: All focus-visible states use tokenized values and appear consistent across buttons, inputs, table rows, and chart interactive elements
Grouped controls (segmented controls, toolbars, checkbox groups) expose a11y-friendly ARIA roles and keyboard flows: arrow-key navigation where appropriate and tab-to-group semantics
Chart legend text and dense table labels meet WCAG AA contrast thresholds against chart backgrounds in default and compact densities
Automated Storybook accessibility snapshots added; CI fails if contrast drops below thresholds for covered stories
VPAT annex notes updated with component-level decisions and test evidence links
tasks: Run a component-level audit: generate a matrix that lists token usage vs actual rendered focus styles
Align design tokens: define focus ring token (focus-ring, focus-outline-width, focus-offset) and publish to tokens spec
Update component guidelines and Figma library with new tokens and examples
Implement ARIA semantics in component library: add aria-roledescription where needed, ensure keyboard arrow handling in groups
Adjust chart legend / table label tokens and validate against color-contrast checker (include disabled/hover/focus states)
Add Storybook stories that exercise keyboard navigation and high-contrast backgrounds
Add axe-core rules to storybook-ci and create gating automation for contrast/aria violations
Prepare VPAT annex: attach screenshots, test logs (NVDA/VoiceOver), and automation output
design_decisions: Use an explicit focus ring token instead of relying on outline:auto; token provides consistent thickness and offset across platforms
For segmented controls, prefer role=tablist/role=tab pattern only when content panels exist; otherwise use a composite radiogroup pattern with aria-checked and arrow-key navigation
Chart legends should default to 4.5:1 for label text; for very small labels (<=12px) fallback to a larger token or an indicator dot + accessible label on hover/focus
Avoid removing visual focus in dense tables; instead reduce padding but preserve minimum 2px focus ring width to maintain visibility
testing_plan: Automated: run axe-core in Storybook CI against all updated stories; capture violations and enforce zero new contrast/aria failures
Manual: NVDA (Windows), VoiceOver (Mac/iOS), and TalkBack (Android) smoke test for representative flows: table keyboard row selection, segmented control arrows, chart legend keyboard focus
Cross-browser: test in Chrome + Firefox + Safari desktop for focus rendering, include High Contrast mode on Windows
Regression: run quick token diff tool to detect any token value drift that would affect focus/contrast
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Token changes may affect other components unexpectedly — Mitigation: release behind feature-flag and run visual diffs for core app pages
Risk: Third-party chart libs may not expose legend styling hooks — Mitigation: create a legend wrapper in our chart foundation layer and document contribution path to upstream when necessary
Risk: Designers/PMs may prefer brand color choices inconsistent with accessibility thresholds — Mitigation: provide alternate token proposals that preserve brand intent while meeting contrast
